    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 13m • 📚 Deep Dive (2611 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Digiday ↗ Open Full Page

    Future of Marketing Briefing: Consulting firms revive their marketing ambitions in the C-suite the holdcos covet

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2611 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Digiday

    ⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 1-3 in Nashville for the Digiday Programmatic Marketing Summit.
    • This Future of Marketing Briefing covers the latest in marketing for Digiday+ members and is distributed over email every Friday at 10 a.m.
    • However the holdcos settle the question of whether the CEO route counts as due diligence, Deloitte Digital and Accenture Song got there first, and both have started selling marketing in the C-suite with a fresh push.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that join us Dec. 1-3 in Nashville for the Digiday Programmatic Marketing Summit.

    This Future of Marketing Briefing covers the latest in marketing for Digiday+ members and is distributed over email every Friday at 10 a.m. ET. More from the series →.

    However the holdcos settle the question of whether the CEO route counts as due diligence, Deloitte Digital and Accenture Song got there first, and both have started selling marketing in the C-suite with a fresh push.

    Deloitte Digital’s offer is Converge, an operating system that strings together AI agents to run marketing and sales work, from research and briefs through to campaign deployment and deal tracking. Some of the agents are Deloitte’s own. Others are ones a client already runs elsewhere, and the whole thing plugs into the tools and clout contracts a brand is already paying for. Marketing and sales versions are live, with commerce on the way, and Deloitte pitches them as one front-office system tied to revenue, which it calls “brand to cash.” Because it’s sold as a license that stretches across sales, marketing and service, it needs sign-off well above the CMO, which suits a consulting firm that’s used to having those conversations.

    Accenture Song’s play in media, a market it has circled in the U.S. for years without committing. In September, it moved Melissa Fein, who built its media planning and buying business in Australia and Newly introduced Zealand after leaving Initiative in 2024, to New York as U.S. media lead. This month it posted a job for a head of media strategy for the Americas. The ad describes a “new world media practice” with no legacy systems to protect, and asks for an AI-first strategist” to lead planning, build new tools and become the person senior clients call before a brief exists.

    Industry observers note that candidates need hands-on command of econometrics, incrementality testing and attribution plus experience in major-spending categories like financial services, telecommunications, automotive and health. Those are the categories where the ANZ team won Australia Post and Mediabank. Accenture Song Ndidi Oteh has kept quiet on specifics, saying only that whatever it does in media won’t take traditional forms.

    It has been revealed that “The real prize is the conversation before the brief,” said  Steve Boehler, founder of agency consultancy the Mercer Island Group. ”If you help define the business problem, design the operating model and decide how success will be measured, you are competing long before an agency review begins.”.

    Both plays echo what the holdcos have spent 18 months engineering: operating systems that run a client’s marketing for it and media businesses that sell more than buying. The consultants may have the better shot at making either one stick. They already sit with the CEOs, CIOs and CFOs who sign off on systems spanning sales, marketing and service and installing that kind of software is their day job. A holdco operating system, rightly or wrongly, still reads as an agency tool, built partly to make the agency cheaper to run. Accenture also arrives in the U.S. media with no legacy buying business to protect, so it can lead with measurement and tools before it has to sell buying power.

    According to recent reports, whether any of this translates is another matter. Consultancies have been trying to crack advertising for the best part of a decade, after all, and the media buying business still rewards a scale Accenture doesn’t yet have in the U.S. Then again, now is arguably as good a time as any for them to try, if not better. With Omnicom and IPG combined, big advertisers are down to three holdcos, and some are skipping the pitch one so a credible alternative has rarely been more useful. AI is also pushing decisions about how marketing works into rooms where the CFO and CIO sit, which consultancies have been in for years. And a C-suite that takes a closer look at marketing will start asking how agencies make their money, from data fees to principal media, which is an awkward question for any firm with a buying business to defend.

    “The consultancies may have an advantage in getting invited to design the system,” remarked Boehler. “That is not the same as proving they can run marketing better. The client still needs evidence of better decisions, better work and better business outcomes, not just fewer handoffs.”.

    Industry observers note that all of which makes the Publicis-WPP episode look a little quaint, partly because it was never quite the fight it was billed as. Sadoun spent months telling investors that Publicis was winning substantial accounts without a pitch. Rose, asked about it by an analyst, called it “this pitchless CEO handshake thing that I keep getting asked about” and said decisions that big deserve careful consideration. Publicis answered with an open letter treating that line as her theory, and the coverage did the rest. Somewhere along the way, a question about how clients choose agencies turned into a row about manners.

    What got lost was the shift both CEOs were describing. Big advertisers are increasingly buying data, identity and AI infrastructure, which a six-week parade of slide decks was never built to judge, so some now test one partner in depth instead of auditioning several. Those decisions are also moving up the organization chart, to executives who sign off on systems not campaigns. That’s how consultancies have always been bought. Deloitte and Accenture are built for long, technical evaluations run by CFOs and CIOs, and while the holdcos; remarks were being turned into a grudge march one rolled out a system that needs the c-suite’s signature and the other started building a U.S. media practice designed to win it.

    According to recent reports, “Client CEOs and CMOs pay attention to CEOs of holdcos, especially when a transition in agency leadership occurs and the agency CEO conducts outreach to key clients,” said Gartner analyst Jay Wilson. “But most recognize that while agency CEOs may set a direction for the agency, that direction may be slow to take hold – or never take hold – within the agency teams doing the actual day-to- day work. A strong relationship with, or aversion to, an agency chief executive is usually more consequential at smaller, independent agencies.”.

    Whatever gets agreed in the c-suite, someone still has to do the work.

    Industry observers note that “The consultants don’t have to copy the incumbent model to compete,” said Boehler. “But they still have to do the work: initiative, negotiate, deliver, reconcile and prove results. A different model is a proposition until clients experience the difference.”.

    Cinema admissions have climbed back on the strength of a fuller blockbuster slate and much of the ad money that shifted to digital during lockdowns stayed put. Most screens still sell their preshow through sales houses that have always sold offline.

    In a recent development, mikkel Hagedorn, a WPP and Omnicom alum, has spent five or six years building a platform that lets buyers book cinema spots programmatically, target them against specific films and count impressions straight off ticket sales. The company is live in Denmark and Finland, where sales houses have handed it two minutes of a 15-minute preshow at a base CPM of around €75. Hagedorn’s bet is that exhibitors can bring cinema into the digital ad market while keeping the premium pricing newspapers gave away when they went programmatic.

    His firm, called Cinemataztic, gives buyers two ways to purchase inventory: first, agencies already running programmatic campaigns can reach the inventory through supply-side platforms and demand-side platforms such as Smartclip Google’s DV360 respectively, which lets cinema sit inside budgets that were going to be spread across other channels anyway, Advertisers who would rather skip the intermediary fees can book directly through Hagedorn’s own interface.

    Either way, the buyer can pick what individual film they want to target, so a brand could run only against the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday movie if it likes. The impressions they buy come straight from exhibitors’ ticketing systems, which means one ticket sold counts as one impression. There are “no multipliers here,” said Hagedorn, a dig at the audience multipliers that inflate numbers elsewhere in media.

    Sources indicate that so far a lot of the money has come from digital agencies edging up the funnel into brand work. Hagedorn said he has seen little cannibalisation of advertisers still buying cinema the old way. He said the business has grown 50% a year and forecasts the same for next year, when the company expands into Sweden, Thailand and a third, bigger market he wouldn’t share.

    Even so, the programmatication of cinema will be a slow burn. Advertising is still its third-largest revenue line after tickets and concessions. Most hand it entirely to sales houses on contracts of three to five years and only learn that demand is falling when the next guarantee shrinks. Hagedorn has been warning them about this for years. “They cannot stay offline forever,” he remarked.

    It has been revealed that brands that gatecrash cultural moments tend to stick to tournaments and royal weddings, and they rarely pick a game that lets players mug strangers in a fake Florida. Grand Theft Auto, the culture-warping franchise, is the exception, and its sixth installment is drawing the kind of guerilla marketing normally reserved for FIFA and the Olympics.

    Anyone trying to keep up can follow the running tally at GTA6Brands.com, an independent tracker run by Mike Litman that logs a fresh stunt each day for his GTA 6 Marketing News podcast. Hardly anything in culture still sets off that kind of scramble across so many brands at once, and with GTA the explanation is scale.

    Recent findings suggest that “I’ve tracked over 290 brand moves around GTA 6 so far, including around 130 unofficial activations,” stated Litman. “That’s a remarkable amount of marketing activity orbiting a product launch, particularly when so many of those brands have no formal relationship with Rockstar. What’s interesting is the range of brands getting involved.”.

    Sources indicate that with media this fragmented, marketers have a shortlist of moments when a mass audience shows up at the same time, and most of those moments involve a ball. GTA earned its spot on that list over 13 years. When GTA 5 launched in 2013 it made $1 billion in three days, which owner Take Two called a rate faster than any other video game, film or other entertainment product has ever managed. For context, Marvel’s “The Avengers” movie took 19 days to reach that number. In the years since it launched, the game has since surpassed 230 million units sold worldwide across three console generations. The wait for the sequel turned into an event of its own. GTA 6’s second trailer received 475 million views across all platforms within 24 hours of its release, beating the 365 million in 24 hours for Marvel’s Deadpool & Wolverine film. Take Two has issued $8 billion for its 2027 guidance for the fiscal year the game introduces in. For a brand that wants a crowd all watching the same thing at once, that’s about as close to a World Cup final as entertainment gets, and nobody has to get past FIFA’s lawyers.

    Sources indicate that “I think the fascinating thing is that GTA 6 has achieved something usually reserved for the World Cup or Super Bowl, but without the stadium, the broadcast rights or the traditional sponsorship machinery,” said Litman. “It’s become a cultural event in its own right. And brands aren’t waiting for permission to participate.”.

    It has been revealed that A few did get permission, though. Rockstar’s list of official partners is short and made up mostly of platforms. Sony signed an exclusive marketing deal, which put a “Plays Best on PS5” tag on the game’s official channels. Netflix got the “Extended Look” trailer six trailers before YouTube in August, in what Take Two boss Strauss Zelnick called a “groundbreaking partnership”. YouTube is running a 24-hour launch live livestream from its own channel, and the Miami Heat have redesigned court, custom uniforms and Vice City merchandise.

    “Nike is going back to its roots and what built the brand: cultural relevance through people who have the trust of a community. It is a bold choice when most advertising pitches are about AI. Nike uses AI too, as a tool, but clearly shows it understands that what stays scarce is trust. Trust comes from identity and proximity: who is speaking, and how close they are to the community listening. It also shows what creators and athletes must build to ask a brand like Nike for more than just a campaign fee. Most of them are offering access to an audience that belongs to a social or tech platform, targeted and measured with the data that the platform makes available. Global stars aside, only those who directly own the relationship with their audience and their data can negotiate a share of the long-term value.”.

    — Alessandro De Zanche, founder of media consultancy ADZ Strategies on Nike’s bet on creators to drive growth.

    $70.7 million: The total amount that U.S. advertisers spent on ChatGPT ads during October.

    Mail Metro Media’s next creator play is representing them Mail Metro Media, the Daily Mail’s ad sales arm, is building an in-house talent agency to represent its creators, which raises an obvious conflict between selling audiences to brands and getting the best deals for the talent.

    Inside Nike’s plan to turn creators into brand buildersNike said it will give creators, local cultural voices, and everyday participants a larger role in building its brand, moving beyond substantial campaigns and superstar deals.

    Skydance’s Rebecca Mall Announces New Marketing Leadership Team

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (563 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Adweek

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, skydance’s marketing division is the latest unit to reveal its new leadership structure.
    • Industry observers note that chief marketing officer Rebecca Mall, in a memo to her team, unveiled the newly introduced vision for the marketing team.
    • She added that the team’s job is not just to market what they create, but also to help drive growth and success for the entire Skydance organization.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, skydance’s marketing division is the latest unit to reveal its new leadership structure. Following its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery in October, Skydance has been busy working to mesh the operations of the two media companies.

    Industry observers note that chief marketing officer Rebecca Mall, in a memo to her team, unveiled the newly introduced vision for the marketing team. “We have an incredible opportunity to build a more unified, innovative and effective marketing organization – one that breaks down silos, understands our audiences better than anyone and harnesses the power of creativity, data and technology to set a new standard for our industry,” according to the memo.

    She added that the team’s job is not just to market what they create, but also to help drive growth and success for the entire Skydance organization.

    Recent findings suggest that mall revealed that cross-manufacturer marketing and corporate brand, data & analytics, media, partnerships, and franchise and kids & family will now be housed under one roof. The upcoming leadership team includes Annah Zafrani, who will be tasked with leading Skydance’s cross-company marketing and brand unit. Zafrani, who comes from Paramount Skydance, will coordinate priority campaigns across the media company’s businesses and lead corporate brand marketing. Reporting to her will be, also from the Paramount Skydance side, Katie Hutchings, svp, brand marketing, creative and strategy, and her team.

    Paramount Skydance’s Angie Sharma will lead franchise and kids & family, building one plan per franchise across content, consumer products, games, and experiences, with kids & family viewed as a key growth priority.

    Recent findings suggest that jamal Salmon, who comes from Paramount Skydance, will lead data & analytics for marketing, and will also report to Josh Goldstine, president of worldwide marketing & distribution, who will also be responsible for film marketing. Salmon will also have a dotted line to Hugh Williams, chief engineer and evp for consumer and monetization engineering; and Josh Walker, chief financial and strategy officer for direct to consumer. The DTC unit oversees streaming and video-on-demand.

    Industry observers note that paramount Skydance’s Michelle Hagen will lead brand partnerships, with Julie Moore, evp of brand partnerships, reporting to her, and Dana Nussbaum, co-head of global motion pictures marketing, Warner Bros., focusing on theatrical. Malene Sam, svp, originals, who was part of Paramount Skydance, report both to Hagen and Shauna Spenley, who leads DTC media. Under Spenley, Sam will be focused on TV and DTC.

    Finally, Seth Goren, who comes from WBD, will lead media, bringing together media strategy, media buying, and agency management across the company. He will report to Mall. But for theatrical media work, he also will report to Nussbaum. For his DTC media work, he will report to Spenley, and for his TV work, he will have a reporting line to Mike Benson, who leads TV Marketing.

    The realignment of the marketing team has led to the departure of Meg Maro, the global head of franchise. Mall thanked her for her contributions during her time at the tech giant.

    Maro concluded saying: “We have an extraordinary opportunity to redefine what marketing can achieve in our industry, and I can’t wait to see what we accomplish together.”.

    Mark Mwachiro is a TVNewser contributor who has been writing for the blog since March 2022. Based out of New York, Mark has also contributed to ADWEEK.

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (759 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Adweek ↗ Open Full Page

    The Art, Science and Theater of Modern Marketing ft. Thomas Ranese

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (759 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Adweek

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • What if the best marketing advantage you have is something that cannot be replicated by an algorithm?
    • For Thomas Ranese, CMO of Intuit, it starts with theater, empathy and understanding what people are actually trying to achieve.
    • In this episode of Marketing Vanguard, Jenny Rooney sits down with Thomas to unpack how an unconventional career spanning theater, Google and Uber shaped his approach to marketing leadership.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    What if the best marketing advantage you have is something that cannot be replicated by an algorithm?

    For Thomas Ranese, CMO of Intuit, it starts with theater, empathy and understanding what people are actually trying to achieve.

    In this episode of Marketing Vanguard, Jenny Rooney sits down with Thomas to unpack how an unconventional career spanning theater, Google and Uber shaped his approach to marketing leadership.

    From growing up behind the counter of his father’s pasta shop to leading marketing at one of the world’s biggest financial technology platforms, Thomas gets into why emotional connection can be just as powerful as performance data.

    He also addresses why AI needs human expertise to earn customer trust, and why brands should bring more humanity, creativity, and purpose into modern marketing.

    Thomas Ranese is Chief Marketing Officer at Intuit, a global technology platform serving millions of customers worldwide with TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma and Mailchimp.

    Sources indicate that his career has taken him through some very different worlds, including theater, consulting, government and nonprofit work, Google and Uber. His approach to marketing is rooted in a simple idea: understand what people are trying to achieve, then build brands and experiences that help them get there. He strongly believes in storytelling and using humor to make complex information more relatable.

    At Intuit, Thomas is helping shape the company’s evolution into an integrated, AI-powered financial technology platform, with a focus on combining technology with human expertise to help consumers and businesses prosper.

    Industry observers note that 07:18 Marketing Is Theater, and It Goes Beyond Advertising — Thomas breaks down the three different kinds of theater that shape modern marketing: the storytelling and drama of advertising, the emotions and interactions built into customer experience, and the immersive experiences brands create through retail. He also believes real-world human interactions will become increasingly important as more of our lives move into digital and AI-powered environments.

    Industry observers note that 12:44 What a Pasta Shop Taught Him About Customer Obsession — Thomas traces his interest in marketing back to his childhood, when he spent time working in his father’s small pasta shop. He loved being behind the counter, helping customers and figuring out what they needed. He even created his father’s first promotional newsletter on a Commodore 64. Looking back, he sees those early experiences as the foundation of his approach to customer connection, communication and service.

    16:01 Why AI Needs Human Intelligence Too — Intuit is building AI into the core of its financial technology platform, but Thomas is particularly focused on the role human experts play alongside it. When customers are making notable decisions about taxes, credit or their businesses, getting the right answer matters. AI can provide powerful technology and efficiency, but human expertise brings verification, empathy and the confidence customers need to act.

    19:57 Money Is a Means to an End. So Is Your Product — Thomas challenges brands to think beyond what their products do and focus on what customers want to achieve with them. Small business owners aren’t necessarily starting businesses because they want to make money; they’re pursuing a craft, building a lifestyle, serving customers or creating opportunities for their families. The same principle applies across categories: brands become more meaningful when they understand the bigger ambitions their products help people achieve.

    Recent findings suggest that 22:00 Intuit’s Goal for Financial Literacy — Thomas explains how Intuit is connecting its mission to power prosperity with financial literacy education. Through Intuit for Education, the manufacturer aims to reach 50 million students by 2030, addressing the fact that only 32% of students graduate able to pass a basic financial literacy exam. For Thomas, this is an opportunity to create meaningful social impact while building trust and introducing a fresh generation to the tools that can help them succeed.

    26:02 Why CMOs Should be Fully Involved — Thomas pushes back on the idea that senior marketing leaders should step away from execution as their organizations grow. With technology and AI changing marketing so quickly, he believes CMOs need to stay hands-on, understand the tools and continue learning. He argues that the bigger the organization, the more crucial this becomes, especially when it is easy to become disconnected from the actual work and the customers being served.

    Jenny Rooney is Chief Brand and Community Officer, leading strategy for the overall ADWEEK brand as well as the ways in which we serve and support our audiences with high-value content, products, partnerships and experiences, notably through our community programs such as Marketing Vanguard.

    The Media RFP Is Quietly Becoming Obsolete ft. Bruce Williams

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Media used to be one part of the marketing machine, but this approach became outdated a while ago.
    • In this episode of Marketing Vanguard, Jenny Rooney sits down with Bruce Williams, CEO of dentsu X North America, to examine how media is becoming the connective tissue across creative, commerce, CRM, data, and technology.
    • Bruce reveals why standalone media RFPs are disappearing, and what it really takes to design connected consumer experiences.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Media used to be one part of the marketing machine, but this approach became outdated a while ago.

    In this episode of Marketing Vanguard, Jenny Rooney sits down with Bruce Williams, CEO of dentsu X North America, to examine how media is becoming the connective tissue across creative, commerce, CRM, data, and technology.

    Bruce reveals why standalone media RFPs are disappearing, and what it really takes to design connected consumer experiences.

    He also addresses why brands need to move from channel-first planning toward operating systems built around outcomes.

    Bruce Williams is CEO of dentsu X North America. Here, his focus is increasingly on helping brands move beyond isolated media planning toward connected operating models that bring together data, content, technology and consumer experience.

    With more than 20 years in media, Bruce has spent much of his career working at the intersection of media strategy, integrated marketing, technology and organizational transformation.

    He also works with clients on AI-enabled transformation, agency interoperability and new ways to turn data into faster decision-making at both global and local levels.

    01:26 The “Media RFP” Is Quietly Becoming Obsolete — Bruce says media RFPs rarely arrive as standalone asks anymore. Brands increasingly want integrated briefs that connect media with creative, experience, CRM and loyalty, or they want agencies to solve bigger transformation problems. So, the agency conversation has to shift from “Can you buy media well?” to “Can you help us operate better?”.

    It has been revealed that 03:13 Your Customer Doesn’t Experience Your Brand in Silos — Marketing may still be organized into separate teams, systems and channels, but the person receiving the experience does not care about those distinctions. Bruce argues that fragmentation remains one of the industry’s longest-running problems because disconnected structures eventually show up as disconnected consumer experiences.

    According to recent reports, 06:22 On AI: Build the System, Then Stay Scrappy — Bruce does not see AI transformation as a choice between massive infrastructure projects and quick tactical wins. He points to work with Heineken that combines long-term data and technology integration with practical tools like local intelligence agents that move competitive and market data directly into local decisions.

    08:51 Why Agencies Can’t Keep Saying “Our Way or Nothing” — For Bruce, the future of agency relationships comes down to interoperability and optionality. Closed systems create friction. Agencies need to work directly with brand data, technology and other partners instead of expecting clients to conform to one proprietary model. Openness is becoming part of the value proposition.

    Jenny Rooney is Chief Brand and Community Officer, leading strategy for the overall ADWEEK brand as well as the ways in which we serve and support our audiences with high-value content, products, partnerships and experiences, notably through our community programs such as Marketing Vanguard.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In the next two years, we aim to help over 250,000 Americans get access to life-changing benefits. Behind that impact is a remarkable group of people — attorneys, engineers, client advocates, marketers, product managers, and more. The Atticus People team makes that work possible — we build the systems, policies and operations that enable us to do our best work.

    We’re hiring a People Operations Lead to run the backbone of our People function: benefits, systems, payroll and multi-state compliance through our PEO, people policy, and our performance and merit cycles. You’ll be the day-to-day owner of how this work gets done — managing our vendors, keeping us compliant as we grow, running our cycles cleanly, and improving the employee experience at every touchpoint. You’ll also play a central role in the bigger decisions ahead of us — when and how we leave our PEO, how we replace our HRIS, how our policies and benefits should evolve — bringing the analysis and recommendations that shape them.

    In a recent development, you’ll report to Amy Yu, our Head of People, and join a small, high-ownership team that cares deeply about our mission and about having real impact. The ideal candidate has run core People Operations programs at a tech-driven organization and is ready to take on a broader scope somewhere the work really matters. We’ve helped hundreds of thousands of people get the benefits they deserve, and the people doing that work are who you’d be building for.

    5+ years in People Operations at a venture-backed tech company, with hands-on ownership of at least a few of: benefits, HRIS, payroll, compliance, performance cycles, and policies.

    You’re equally comfortable running a benefits analysis as you are having a tough leave conversation, and handle both with tact and clarity.

    You’ve administered an HRIS end-to-end and managed People vendors and partners; you’ve driven a system implementation or migration and know what makes one go well.

    You’ve automated and improved HR processes to be more efficient, accurate and seamless for both HR and business consumers.

    You operate with low ego but high ownership, and are comfortable both doing the work and figuring out how it can be improved.

    The role is a rare opportunity to join a fast-growing Series C startup that doubles as a B-corp social enterprise. Our team is still small enough for you to have an outsized impact on how we operate and how our people experience unfolds.

    We offer competitive pay — including equity — and generous benefits:.

    Medical and dental insurance with 100% of employee and family premiums covered.

    15 vacation days & ~20 paid holidays each year (including two weeks at end-of-year).

    $1,000 reimbursable stipend for education and training outside of work.

    Up to $1,200/year student loan repayment assistance.

    Humble, thoughtful, smart, fun colleagues.

    According to recent reports, we anticipate the base salary band for this role will be between $120,000 to $160,000 in addition to equity and benefits. The salary at offer will be determined by a number of factors such as candidate’s experience, knowledge, skills and abilities, as well as internal equity among our team.

    Recent findings suggest that this job is fully remote and we’re committed to empowering everyone with flexibility. Work remotely, and travel to LA (on the organization dime) as needed to be with your colleagues – usually quarterly, plus offsites. We care a lot about building a great culture and we think some interactions need to happen in person, so we put a lot of thought into retreats, offsites, and other ways to gather.

    Industry observers note that supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

    We’re seeking a Customer Solutions Architect (CSA) to help drive the adoption of Supabase across a diverse range of customers: from agile startups building towards their first launch to established brands with highly scaled workloads.

    At Supabase, CSA’s are responsible for the entire customer journey, working closely with our most valuable users to:.

    Uncover and understand business and technical requirements.

    Design and architect technical solutions built on the Supabase platform.

    Work with customers to lead proof-of-value implementations.

    Provide regular customer engagements to answer complex questions, unblock adoption, and optimize scaled performance.

    Successful CSAs always put customers first, working closely with them to become trusted advisors who understand their needs, work as an extension of their team toward common success, and advocate on behalf of the customer within Supabase.

    You'll be joining our team to support Supabase Team & Enterprise customers, where you will be expected to lead and innovate around the following areas of responsibility:.

    Lead technical discovery to uncover business and technical objectives, set appropriate expectations of the Supabase platform, and define the criteria for success, ensuring customers can receive the guidance they need to achieve it.

    Design, build, and present Supabase platform demonstrations to high-value customers. Leverage quality storytelling to present the value of the Supabase platform and of the entire Supabase Success team.

    Work directly with Growth team members to size deals, provide anticipated usage estimates, and identify potential workloads supported by the Platform.

    Collaborate directly with customers to determine the technical scope of a proof-of-value to ensure customers recognize the value of the Supabase platform while minimizing risk to adoption.

    Set proof-of-value timelines, business outcomes, and success criteria that ensure a customer is comfortable proceeding with the platform once a proof-of-value has been completed.

    Actively guide new customers through an onboarding journey, utilizing emails, docs, guides, and webinars to promote their rapid deployment and growth on the platform.

    Understand immediate custom goals (i.e onboard and adoption) as well as long-term customer opportunities (i.e. optimization & identifying new workloads) to build meaningful account plans for high-value customers.

    Deliver on synchronous and asynchronous engagements with Supabase customers, including application architecture assessments, database design and performance optimization, and proactive support to enable customers to scale with confidence.

    Serve as an internal champion for your customers and for the platform. Work closely with Support, Product, and Engineering to provide platform feedback, identify areas of improvement, while communicating platform roadmaps to customers.

    Industry observers note that invest in customer connections to build a trust-based relationship. Everyday CSA’s work with the production data stores of startups and enterprises alike. Building trust in the Success team and Supabase platform is paramount to a successful customer relationship.

    6+ years of relevant work experience in Solutions Architecture, Database Engineering, or similar.

    Strong background with relational database management systems such as PostgreSQL or MySQL.

    Background in web application development, with familiarity with Python, C# and popular JavaScript frameworks (React, Vue, Svelte) as well as Node.js.

    Industry observers note that very strong communication skills, particularly of technical concepts. CSA’s at Supabase spend a significant amount of time translating business needs to technical outcomes, and technical concepts to organizational impact.

    Recent findings suggest that well-organized and effective storyteller with meaningful interpersonal skills. CSA’s often have to navigate multiple stakeholders with conflicting opinions, and the ability to effectively mediate this type of conflict is crucial.

    Industry observers note that experience with project management, business analysis and revenue operations tools. We use HubSpot, BigQuery etc., and familiarity with these platforms will help enable your success.

    Previous experience leading customer-facing engagements to deliver meaningful technical and business value.

    Recent findings suggest that we hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

    Recent findings suggest that every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the manufacturer. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

    Recent findings suggest that supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

    Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

    We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

    According to recent reports, supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

    Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F).

    Recent findings suggest that we move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

    According to recent reports, our customers trust us with audio, video and data belonging to their own end people, so a security failure on our side puts their data and their business at risk. We are hiring an Infrastructure Security Engineer to improve the security posture of the production platform that carries that data. You will join a small Trust team that covers security, IT and compliance, and you will own real parts of the program from your first week. You will build our understanding of infrastructure security posture, then prioritize and drive remediation by business impact. Where the same class of problem keeps coming back, you will build the guardrails and security building blocks that let our security scale with the business.

    translate security concerns into engineering action.

    are a fast learner and thrive in ambiguity.

    Map the security posture of our cloud and production infrastructure and turn it into a documented baseline.

    Find the gaps that could lead to customer data loss or infrastructure compromise, agree a prioritized security debt backlog with engineering, and close the highest-risk items first.

    Harden identity, secrets and network boundaries, including cloud IAM, environment separation and credential hygiene.

    Secure the infrastructure that runs customer-deployed voice AI agents: tenant isolation, secrets for third-party model providers, and media and recording storage.

    Build guardrails and secure defaults into our infrastructure as code so the secure path is the easy one for engineers.

    Partner with our Compliance team to map infrastructure controls to PCI-DSS and ISO 27001 and automate the technical evidence those audits depend on.

    5+ years in security engineering, infrastructure engineering or SRE, with a significant share of that focused on infrastructure security.

    Hands-on experience securing a major cloud provider (AWS, GCP or Azure) and containerized workloads including Kubernetes.

    A track record of owning infrastructure security for a production platform.

    Fluency with infrastructure as code such as Terraform, and strong scripting and automation skills in a language such as Go or Python.

    A pragmatic approach to risk: you can explain why a finding matters to the business and how fast it needs to be fixed.

    Experience with real-time media, networking or WebRTC systems.

    Experience in AI security, such as securing LLM applications or agent infrastructure.

    Incident response or application security experience.

    Experience supporting compliance audits such as PCI-DSS, ISO 27001, SOC 2 or HIPAA.

    An opportunity to build something truly impactful to the world.

    Contribute to open source alongside world-class engineers.

    Competitive salary and equity package.

    Health, dental, and vision benefits.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers.
    • Container Engineering (ConEng) owns the internal container platform that runs Supabase's multi-tenant, multi-region services — the managed Kubernetes platform that other engineering teams build and deploy on top of.
    • Your job is to make the platform itself trustworthy, observable, and cheap to operate at scale — and to raise the reliability bar for everyone who depends on it.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth. More than 9 million developers and 250,000+ customers now build on Supabase, and the majority of latest databases on the platform are created by AI app builders — so the systems underneath have to stay reliable while they grow fast.

    Container Engineering (ConEng) owns the internal container platform that runs Supabase's multi-tenant, multi-region services — the managed Kubernetes platform that other engineering teams build and deploy on top of. We own cluster lifecycle and cluster classes, multi-cluster and multi-region topology, capacity, scheduling, isolation and runtime safety, the higher-level platform APIs, the Kubernetes deployment contract and Argo semantics, rollout primitives, and runtime configuration and secret injection.

    Your job is to make the platform itself trustworthy, observable, and cheap to operate at scale — and to raise the reliability bar for everyone who depends on it. This is not a gatekeeper role. You'll make the reliable path the easy path: building the automation and platform APIs that let product teams run safely by default, instrumenting what we operate, and making sure that when something breaks we detect it and recover fast.

    The work spans three strength areas:.

    Tooling & ecosystem — deep knowledge of the container and orchestration landscape (Kubernetes, containerd/OCI, the CNCF ecosystem) and a clear point of view on how to compose it.

    Software engineering — designing and building the platform's automation, controllers, and internal tooling as production code, including solutions that don't come pre-shaped by an existing tool.

    Operational / SRE practice — the discipline (SLOs, error budgets, incident response, ORRs) that runs the platform at scale as a predictable one.

    In a recent development, we expect you to be genuinely deep in at least one of these, and many of our strongest candidates are deep in two (usually leaning toward one). Bringing real strength across all three is rare and exceptional — and even then, no one is equally strong in all three at once, so you'd focus where you're most needed at any given time. Different profiles are welcome here; tell us which of these is your center of gravity.

    Regardless of the skill set, all team members carry a share of the team's on-call rota, responding to platform incidents and driving them to resolution and follow-up.

    Platform reliability & operations.

    Define SLIs/SLOs and error budgets for the container platform itself, and build error-budget policies that actually gate platform changes.

    Own the Operational Readiness Review (ORR) process for latest platform capabilities and major changes.

    Design and track metrics for platform uptime, and increase observability into the platform by capturing the right metrics, logs, and traces across the platform layers.

    Drive the incident-to-improvement pipeline: facilitate blameless postmortems, connect findings to readiness gaps, spot repeat failure patterns, and push through systemic fixes.

    Build and maintain the platform's automation, controllers, operators, and internal tooling — writing production code and shipping it, not just wiring together existing tools.

    Design and implement the platform-side CI/CD and rollout primitives that speed up platform deployments while working within proper change and release management.

    Implement and maintain security automation for the platform: intrusion detection, automated remediation, and patch management.

    Identify and quantify operational toil, and build the automation that removes it rather than just documenting it.

    Contribute to the platform's continual testing automation — the test suites and pipelines that validate platform releases are fit for purpose before they reach tenants.

    Tooling, ecosystem & architecture.

    Act as a platform reliability and architecture expert — contribute to failure-mode analysis, dependency mapping, and resilience design for multi-tenant container workloads.

    Evaluate and evolve the platform's tooling ecosystem (orchestration, runtime, networking, isolation, and observability stack) with a clear, opinionated view on trade-offs.

    Improve system architecture to reduce infrastructure cost while balancing security, reliability, and performance across tenants.

    Guide teams building on the platform to design sustainable on-call practices for their own services: alert quality, escalation paths, runbook coverage, and noise reduction.

    Have 5+ years in platform engineering, container/Kubernetes platform operations, SRE, or production infrastructure, and have operated production systems at scale and carried on-call for them.

    Are genuinely deep in at least one — ideally two — of the three strength areas below (and tell us which is your center of gravity):.

    Tooling & ecosystem — know the container/orchestration landscape well: Kubernetes, containerd and the OCI/CRI standards, and the surrounding CNCF ecosystem (e.g. Argo CD/Argo Rollouts for GitOps and progressive delivery; Cilium/eBPF networking and the Gateway API; Karpenter/KEDA-style autoscaling; and workload-isolation runtimes such as gVisor or Kata Containers). You reason about trade-offs rather than reaching for defaults.

    Software engineering — write real production code (Go and/or a comparable systems language) and can build controllers, operators, and platform APIs — stepping back to the underlying problem and building the right solution when no off-the-shelf tool fits.

    Operational / SRE practice — are fluent in SLOs, error budgets, and operational KPIs; have led incident response and blameless postmortems; and have driven down MTTD/MTTR for systems you operated.

    Have worked with large-scale multi-tenant systems and understand isolation as a spectrum — from namespaces, RBAC, network policies, and resource quotas through to stronger primitives such as virtual clusters (e.g. vCluster) or VM-class runtimes.

    Operate confidently on AWS (multiple accounts, IAM, VPC) and are comfortable with infrastructure-as-code (Pulumi preferred; Terraform/CDK also fine) and Kubernetes.

    Script and automate to eliminate toil rather than absorb it.

    Communicate clearly with both infrastructure specialists and product engineers, and thrive in async, globally distributed teams.

    Are comfortable navigating ambiguity and iterating toward better systems over time.

    Experience building and operating a multi-tenant Kubernetes platform that internal teams deploy onto.

    Familiarity with policy engines (Kyverno, or OPA/Gatekeeper) and cost-attribution tooling (OpenCost/Kubecost) for per-tenant chargeback/showback.

    Experience with managed database platforms or Postgres.

    Familiarity with OpenTelemetry, Prometheus/VictoriaMetrics, Grafana, or similar observability tooling.

    • Our beginning: A world that enjoys economic freedom and wealth protection,no matter where you live or who is running your country.To achieve that, we search the world for the best people for the job.
    • Although we are headquartered in Gibraltar, this is a full time, 100% remote position Work from anywhere!
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Diversity is at the heart of who we are at Xapo Bank. We’re a fully distributed team of over 160 Xapiens that work remotely from 50+ countries around the world.

    Our beginning: A world that enjoys economic freedom and wealth protection,no matter where you live or who is running your country.To achieve that, we search the world for the best people for the job. We work hard, think globally, and inspire each other to learn and grow. We are committed to changing the way things are done.

    Although we are headquartered in Gibraltar, this is a full time, 100% remote position Work from anywhere!

    Xapo's product suite has grown from a Bitcoin vault into a full member proposition: BTC and USD accounts that pay interest, a global card with Bitcoin cashback, Bitcoin-backed loans, a growing suite of BTC wealth and credit products, and access to stocks, ETFs, and stablecoins, all inside one regulated relationship.

    Xapo is a bank, and a bank earns on the money its members choose to hold with it. Each of those products shipped well. What hasn't yet existed is a single owner of the economics of the customer relationship: one person accountable for winning the right members, growing what they hold with us, and keeping them, and for the balance-sheet products that make that possible.

    In a recent development, the Chief Customer Officer is a new role at the top of the house, reporting to the CEO. You will run the stream that grows what members hold with Xapo, and you will own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional. It brings growth, client coverage, product management, and product design under one leader who is judged on customer contribution, the assets attracted and kept, and the members who stay. This is a customer-focused role in the most commercial sense: what a member earns from us, not the feature we shipped, is the centre of every decision.

    The measure of success is a Customer P&L that grows on what members hold and keep: LTV:CAC improving, approved-to-paid rising, churn falling, and customer contribution the business can plan against.

    This is a banking role, not a requirements-gathering role, a marketing role, or a role you can run from a dashboard. Products are priced on the balance sheet and judged on the money they attract and keep.

    Recent findings suggest that this part matters as much as the mandate. The known failure mode for this role, in any firm, is a CCO with a polished customer-insight deck and no ownership of the number. That is disqualifying here.

    In a recent development, day 30: The Customer P&L baseline is documented across retail and institutional: customer contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, net paid-member growth, and assets attracted and kept. You have formed your own independent view of where members are won, lost, and under-served, and shared it with the CEO and Board.Day 60: The unified Customer operating model is live: one set of key results across Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design, read weekly from one source. Every mission PM owns a product's contribution and its price, and the roadmap is ranked on what it earns, built with Finance and the line leads.Day 90: At least one measurable improvement in LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, or net upcoming AUM flow is live and attributable to a change you made, not a feature ship, an outcome moved. Every cell in your line has defined key results and an owner who explains the number every week.

    Impact Globally, Work Remotely.

    Shape the FutureImprove lives through cutting-edge technology, work 100% remotely from anywhere in the world.

    Sources indicate that great work-life balanceBuild amazing things with a balance of autonomy and collaborative teamwork. Set your own work schedule and make use of a flexible PTO initiative when you need to recharge.

    Expect ExcellenceCollaborate, learn, and grow with a high-performance team. Learn how you learn best - from books to conferences, you’ll get a yearly budget for your individual learning and development goals.

    At Xapo, we prioritize consumer protection and adhere to regulatory requirements by ensuring that all Xapiens are accountable for upholding principles of fair treatment, transparency, and ethical conduct in their interactions with customers and stakeholders.

    According to recent reports, liveKit is building the infrastructure layer for the voice-driven era of computing.     According to recent reports, A lot of technical recruiting jobs at startups are a sprint: a significant hiring push, a pile of reqs, then a hiring freeze and a reorg. This isn't that. Our engineering hiring is steady and it's going to stay that way, so we want someone who'd rather go deep with a handful of engineering teams than churn through whatever's on fire this week. The tradeoff: you'll be expected to actually understand what you're hiring for and how your work impacts the business overall. You'll be a Talent Business Partner to the LiveKit team.

    You'll thrive as a Senior Technical Recruiter if you:.

    are known as the go-to person for tackling tough problems.

    are focused on polish, detail and quality.

    are a fast learner, frequently picking up fresh tips, tricks, and skills.

    Own 8-10 engineering and technical searches end to end, from kickoff to signed offer.

    Partner with engineering hiring managers on what the role really needs, and push back when the requirements don't match the market.

    Source hard: find the infra, backend, SDK, and AI engineers who aren't looking, and give them a reason to talk to us.

    Understand what candidates are motivated by and create a strategy to get them there.

    Build pipelines for the roles we hire for again and again, so new reqs don't start from zero.

    Run an honest, authentic and clear process emphasizing candidate experience that people talk about, even the ones we don't hire.

    Help build the systems the Talent team runs on, from sourcing playbooks to interview kits.

    5+ years of full-cycle technical recruiting, mostly in-house.

    You've owned senior and staff-level engineering searches and closed them.

    You can hold a real conversation with an engineer about their work.

    You source proactively and know how to build and sustain a strong bench.

    You've recruited for infrastructure, developer tools, open source, or AI companies.

    You've built or rebuilt a recruiting process from scratch.

    You know how to win top talent, even when competing against offers from big tech.

    You've used Ashby and Gem (or have strong opinions about the tools you did use).

    Have a degree or certificate in computer science.

    Have experience with executive recruiting.

    An opportunity to build something truly impactful to the world.

    Competitive salary and equity package.

    Health, dental, and vision benefits.

    It has been revealed that most AE roles ask you to sell a product you only half understand to buyers who already know they want it. This is not that role. You'll sell a deeply technical product to developers, CTOs, and product teams — people who can smell a script from a mile away and will respect you more for going deep on the tech than for any closing line you've practiced. We don't have a polished playbook handed down from a head of sales who left three companies ago. We have a latest sales leader, a market that's exploding faster than we can keep up with, and a real opportunity for the right person to help define the motion from the inside.

    If you're energized by ambiguity, allergic to bureaucracy, and the kind of seller who genuinely enjoys learning why a customer is building what they're building — keep reading.

    You'll thrive as an Account Executive if you:.

    are obsessed with making the best product for our customers.

    are known as the go-to person for tackling tough problems.

    work hard and can build and ship fast.

    are focused on polish, detail and quality.

    are a fast learner, frequently picking up newly introduced tips, tricks, and skills.

    The best way to impress us is with thoughtful ways you'd implement LiveKit, and potentially tinkering with it 😊.

    Own and manage the full sales cycle, from prospecting and discovery to demos, negotiation, and close.

    Develop deep product understanding and communicate technical value to developers, CTOs, and product teams.

    Generate pipeline through outbound efforts and strategic partnerships, with support from marketing and sales development.

    Build and maintain strong relationships with prospects and customers, identifying their goals and how our platform helps them succeed.

    Collaborate with Product and Engineering to bring customer feedback into roadmap discussions and positioning.

    Help shape and evolve our sales playbook, messaging, and GTM motion as one of the earliest sales hires.

    Accurately forecast and track pipeline activity, working closely with leadership to inform strategy and planning.

    4+ years of full-cycle SaaS sales experience, with at least 2 of those years selling into enterprise.

    A track record of consistently selling 6-figure deals and hitting or exceeding quota in fast-paced or early-stage environments.

    Strong instincts for selling technical products — APIs, developer tools, or infrastructure tooling — you don't shy away from going deep with technical buyers.

    Comfortable in low-process, high-autonomy environments and bringing structure where it's missing.

    Able to translate technical capability into business value for both technical buyers and executive stakeholders.

    High accountability, ownership, and bias for action — you don't wait to be told what the right next move is.

    Disciplined with CRM and pipeline hygiene (HubSpot, Salesforce, etc.).

    Experience selling at an infrastructure or developer-tools tech giant, ideally with multi-product or platform sales motion.

    Time spent as one of the earliest sellers at a startup — you know what it feels like to build the plane while flying it.

    A real interest in voice AI, agents, or real-time infrastructure (not just "AI" in your LinkedIn headline).

    You once spent a Saturday building something with an API just to see if you could 😏.

    An opportunity to build something truly impactful to the world.

    Uscreen is the video monetization platform for businesses building recurring revenue from video content. Our customers replace a patchwork stack of separate hosting, community, courses, email, and app vendors with one branded experience across web, mobile, and TV.

    The platform is only half of it. We believe growth requires behavior, not just software. Customers don't stall because a feature is missing. They stall because they priced wrong, never built an email list, or introduced an offer nobody wanted. Coaching is how we fix that, and it's part of the product rather than an add-on.

    You own a segment, and you run it like a growth marketer.

    According to recent reports, we have a cohort of smaller video businesses where retention is not where it should be. Nobody owns it today. You will. The revenue that stays in that segment, and the revenue that grows inside it, is yours.

    It has been revealed that this is a coaching role for someone with a growth marketer's mindset. We wouldn't hire a demand gen marketer who couldn't analyze the state of the business and figure out what's needed, and we won't hire a coach who can't either. You'll look at a customer's business the way an owner would: where the revenue comes from, where it leaks, and what to do next. You pull your own numbers to get there. When a customer needs a custom report to answer a growth question, you build it yourself.

    Recent findings suggest that it's a one-to-many job. Your cohort is larger than a 1:1 book, so the work is designing coaching that scales: cohort programs, group sessions, office hours, and triggered outreach when the data says a business is drifting. You'll build that motion rather than inherit it.

    Sources indicate that success is measured in dollars: gross revenue retention in your cohort first, expansion second. Not tickets closed, not calls booked.

    Recent findings suggest that A coach with a growth marketer's mindset. Maybe you've run growth or demand gen for a small business, built your own audience, or coached founders through their numbers. You understand how a membership business makes money, you pull your own analytics to see what's working, and you're comfortable doing it in front of a client. What matters is that you can find the real constraint in a business, then sit with the operator and say the honest thing.

    Ability to execute highly complex and ambiguous projects, working across business strategy and marketing tactics.

    Track record of running creative testing as an always on pipeline, consistently shipping new concepts to prevent performance decay and unlock incremental scale.

    • It’s the chance to define a new category : The Operating System (OS) for Human Greatness Augmented with AI.

    • You’ll be working with the most complex data in the world : the human mind.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    This isn’t another product job.

    It’s the chance to define a new category : The Operating System (OS) for Human Greatness Augmented with AI.

    According to recent reports, science-backed. Design-led. AI-powered. Global.

    A chance to build an AI-native Product Department.

    You’ll be working with the most complex data in the world : the human mind.

    Deep inside you are looking for a fresh adventure with….

    🚀Ambition around AI field : Smart teammates driven to create an iconic, international product.

    🔥Impact : you strive to make a real difference in the company's growth, and not be a number in a big organization.

    😍Mission : knowing your greatness left a mark in people's lives, through technology and behavioral science.

    At Paradox, we believe that greatness is trainable.

    That’s why we want to empower people at scale by leveraging cutting edge technologies like AI, and crafting user experiences with outstanding aesthetics.

    - Human Intelligence (coaches, peers, and mentors).

    - Structured Intelligence (protocols, mental models, rituals),.

    - Technological Intelligence (AI personalization, feedback loops, adaptive journeys).

    To create one seamless ecosystem: Paradox OS.

    This is why we are looking for a PM to make Paradox a category-defining global brand loved for its product.

    This is a full-time position from our beautiful offices in Dubai, Paris or Lisbon or remotely anywhere in the world.

    We believe self-help is broken.Most learning platforms are used the same way : consuming generic theories, getting quick highs, ending with no real change.

    At Paradox, we believe people deserve more.More than content. More than motivation.

    They deserve a system that knows them, one that adapts, challenges, and grows with them.

    We believe that every human learns differently, and that technology can do more than entertain or save time.It can translate insight into transformation, through AI personalization, lean experimentation, and deep psychological understanding.

    Because learning shouldn’t just make you feel inspired for a day, it should change how you live, think, and create.

    At Paradox, we want to re-invent how people grow.

    We do not build another course or coaching app but the Operating System for Greatness.

    Founded by David Laroche - a creator followed by over 2 million people and known for his interviews with icons like Tony Parker, Mike Horn, Richard Branson, and Gad Elmaleh, Paradox aims to build something that will live beyond any individual (including its founder), for decades to come.

    Our ambition is to compete with players like Mindvalley (150M ARR), but with a sharper vision, grounded protocols for achievers, people who want more for their life, refusing mediocrity.

    To do that, we bring together designers, tech, coaches, and filmmakers to create learning experiences that are cinematic, precise, and effective.

    According to recent reports, we move fast, aim high, and hold ourselves to the standards of Apple, Spotify, and MasterClass. No fluff, focused on meaningful impact.

    While others hide their numbers, we want to let our results speak loudly for us.

    Get obsessed with transforming our clients’ lives and let those transformations be our marketing.

    We want to build an AI-native firm, with agents in every department doing the work alongside our people.

    In product, that means building a self-learning AI for product management: a system that learns from every user signal, experiment and release, and gets sharper at deciding what to build next.

    For our clients, it means a self-learning AI that serves them through psychology and coaching, and gets better at helping each person change with every interaction.

    You won’t just use AI tools: you’ll help design the agents, loops and feedback systems that make Paradox learn faster than anyone else.

    -----------------------------------------.

    As Product Manager, you’ll be the architect of a newly introduced category, transforming growth into a living ecosystem powered by AI, behavioral science, and design.

    You won’t just build features, you’ll craft experiences that rewire behavior.

    You’re the architect bringing clarity between vision and execution, the person who turns “we should build this” into “it’s live, here’s the data and tangible impact.”.

    Every product cycle you lead will integrate:.

    Protocols : guided frameworks grounded in psychology that rewire perception, emotion, and action.

    Pods : human connection, accountability, and shared rituals.

    Loops : adaptive, AI-powered coaching cycles that evolve with each user.

    Personalization : experiences that feel uniquely theirs, every time.

    It has been revealed that going from a successful personal brand, to an international tech-driven iconic brand, is far from easy. It will be messy, chaotic - requiring constant iterations on MVPs and innovation in tech. Therefore to achieve this here are :.

    -----------------------------------------.

    Translate the founder’s strategic vision into a clear product strategy.

    Build and maintain the roadmap that connects business goals, user outcomes, and technological innovation.

    Ensure every feature supports the evolution of the Paradox ecosystem: Loops, PX Agents, Protocols, Membership.

    Be obsessed with user problems : talk to users weekly, analyze patterns, and identify where transformation breaks.

    Turn insights from behavioral science, coaching psychology, and learning design into actionable product hypotheses.

    Design loops, feedback, and rituals that make growth tangible.

    build for both the heart (inspiration) and the brain (structure).

    Apply Lean Startup methodology and scientific thinking to validate ideas through MVPs, not opinions.

    Design experiments and measurable success metrics before building.

    Iterate on a weekly basis on newly introduced hypothesis.

    Define and track product success metrics (activation, retention, transformation rates).

    Connect data to business KPIs, know how your product drives lifetime value, not just engagement.

    We don’t track metrics just for internal dashboards, we track them also to prove transformation.

    Help marketing leverage this data to fuel authentic, evidence-based storytelling — showing the world what real transformation looks like.

    Create a visceral experience that translates into emotions of inspiration, awe from users.

    Use a Science-backed, Cinematic, Contrarian style : Every product touchpoint should be grounded in behavioral science, expressed with cinematic beauty, and challenge conventions.

    -----------------------------------------.

    3–6 years as a Product Manager / Product Owner in EdTech, SaaS, or Consumer Tech.

    Bonus: experience in AI-driven products, learning design, or personal development platforms.

    You’ve shipped at least one major feature or product end-to-end, and can show measurable results.

    Uses Figma comfortably, prototypes directly.

    Craft-obsessed : You get things done, you love to work much beyond 9-5, you have a doer mentality, a bias for outcomes and want to be a beast in your field.

    User & Impact Obsessed: You think in outcomes, not outputs, you care about transformation.

    Analytical & System Thinker: You can turn a vague problem into a clear hypothesis, metrics, and roadmap.

    Digital & AI savvy : you’re able to build AI Agents (if not, you demonstrate ability to learn while applying).

    Cross-disciplinary Curiosity: You speak both tech and human; You can move from vision to spreadsheet to Figma.

    English: Fluent English, you can hold a conversation on specific details with English-speaking colleagues.

    Our chosen language for written communication is English.

    --------------------------------.

    ❌ If you need clarity before chaos — wrong place.❌ If you prefer balance over intensity — wrong season.❌ If you build to deliver, not to elevate — wrong mission.

    ❌Surface-level Vision Alignment : you like the idea of Paradox but doesn’t want to get the depth. Paradox is design-led; you must touch the product, not just manage it.

    ✅ If you’re obsessed with systems, psychology, and design…✅ If you dream of using AI to amplify what makes us human….

    Build a product that fuses neuroscience, design, and AI to reinvent how humans grow.

    The chance to build a product that could redefine human potential.

    Work with filmmakers, psychologists, engineers, and creatives obsessed with impact.

    In the heart of our headquarters stands the 100 000 Dreams Wall,.

    Every photo on that wall is a life rewritten:.

    “I found peace with my father.”.

    You will play a crucial role in the development of an Iconic Product.

    -> 🏅Being surrounded by A-players who strive to perform.

    But you don’t just want a competitive paycheck, you also want….

    -> Playing a crucial role in the development of a firm whose content and products will be used by millions of people.

    -> Waking up in the morning feeling like you are making a difference is something!We receive messages every day from clients who have successfully lost weight, quit smoking, reached a milestone in their business, built better relationships, and made positive changes in their lives.

    -> ❤️ Contributing to the Paradox Foundation (our non-profit), dedicated to empower teenagers.

    But that's not all, we believe that driven people deserve….

    -> 😎A manufacturer culture based on autonomy & accountability.

    -> 🌎A remote culture from day one with the freedom to work from wherever you want.

    -> 🏤Magnificent office in Dubai, Paris, Lisbon - it feels like home :).

    -> 🧍‍♀️Standing desks paid by the manufacturer if you live far from our offices.

    -> 💻Work on Mac, for us it counts :).

    -> 🏀350€ per year paid by the tech giant to take care of yourself ( for your gym, or dance class or whatever make you feel great).

    -> 📚150€ of books or education - At Paradox, we are learner lovers and we want to support you in that.

    -> 🔥6 1:1coachings - A Paradox Coach supporting you on anything personal or professional, we want you to live your best life.

    ⚠️ To complete the recruitment process, each candidate must organize calls with his or her previous managers. If you are not comfortable with this : do not apply ⚠️.

    If all this sounds good to you, come and write the next chapter with us 🚀🚀🚀🚀.

    That job description resonated with you?

    Here is your tailor made hiring process.

    📃 A 6 to 8 minutes application survey (with a short video assignment).

    💻 A 30mn video call with Timy, HR, to deep dive into your career path and ambitions.

    💻 A 1h video call with Timy, HR, to discuss how you'd fit into Paradox’s Product team.

    💻 A 1h culture-fit video call, to assess alignment with our values and mindset.

    💻 A 1h final video call with David, CEO, to discuss Product Vision and the next milestones to build.

    💼 Reference check to understand how you operate across environments and help set you up for a smooth onboarding.

    In a recent development, our recruitment process is tailored to do our best to avoid that you or us realize that we’re not a perfect fit. Every step serves a purpose and will allow us to get to know you better as much as it’ll help you understand more where you’ll be stepping in.

    We also want you to have time to ask all of your questions regarding the mission, the long-term vision of your team and the manufacturer, our values, with the relevant interlocutor in front of you.

    If you believe design and AI can awaken what’s best in us then this isn’t a career move.

    Let’s build the Operating System for Greatness.

    You’ve shipped at least one major feature or product end-to-end, and can show measurable results.

    Uses Figma comfortably, prototypes directly.

    Craft-obsessed : You get things done, you love to work much beyond 9-5, you have a doer mentality, a bias for outcomes and want to be a beast in your field.

    User & Impact Obsessed: You think in outcomes, not outputs, you care about transformation.

    Analytical & System Thinker: You can turn a vague problem into a clear hypothesis, metrics, and roadmap.

    Digital & AI savvy : you’re able to build AI Agents (if not, you demonstrate ability to learn while applying).

    Cross-disciplinary Curiosity: You speak both tech and human; You can move from vision to spreadsheet to Figma.

    English: Fluent English, you can hold a conversation on specific details with English-speaking colleagues.

    Our chosen language for written communication is English.

    ✅ If you’re obsessed with systems, psychology, and design…✅ If you dream of using AI to amplify what makes us human….

    Work with filmmakers, psychologists, engineers, and creatives obsessed with impact.

    Every photo on that wall is a life rewritten:.

    You will play a crucial role in the development of an Iconic Product.

    -> 🏅Being surrounded by A-players who strive to perform.

    -> Playing a crucial role in the development of a company whose content and products will be used by millions of people.

    -> 😎A organization culture based on autonomy & accountability.
